subject: Capacity commitment timeline, GPU pool sizing and fallback clauses
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stratushealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stratushealth.com
Date: 2025-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP for Dedicated/Private (GPU lead times)

Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to get a concrete mutual action plan (MAP) that calls out:
- expected lead times for Dedicated vs Private deployment (we need H100-equivalent within a 12–16 week window),
- recommended GPU pool sizing to support our 250K monthly token peak, and
- fallback/credit terms if there are >10% sustained latency regressions during onboarding.

Can you send a one-pager MAP that we can take to our legal and procurement this week? The timeline is tight — our board sign-off window is end of May.

Sincerely,
Daniel Park
Director of AI Infrastructure
StratusHealth

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stratushealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP for Dedicated/Private (GPU lead times)

Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've sketched a short MAP and attached an editable workbook (MAP_StratusHealth_v1.xlsx). High level summary below; workbook has the milestone table and acceptance criteria you can paste into procurement: 

Key proposal (summary):
- Target close window: 4–6 weeks to contract signature (overlap with SOC2 evidence exchange).
- Provisioning lead times: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool on Redwood-hosted infra) — baseline 10–12 weeks to deliver committed tranche of 8 x H100-equivalent nodes; Private (VPC/on‑prem) — 14–18 weeks depending on site readiness and rack/cabling scheduling.
- Recommended initial GPU pool sizing: 8 nodes (H100-equivalent) to meet 250K token peaks with burst headroom; we recommend a 2x burst buffer (autoscale reserve) for first 60 days.
- Acceptance & rollback: three acceptance gates (smoke, perf, stability). If average token latency degradation >10% for 3 consecutive days during the stability gate, Redwood will trigger fallback to a compatible model variant + 15% unit-credit to offset impact while remediation is completed.

Immediate next steps:
1) Review attached MAP workbook and confirm milestone dates in column B.
2) Procurement/legal to confirm contract SLA/credit language; we can propose a short schedule for DocuSign to match your board window.

I've copied Ben and Neha to align on pool sizing and lead-time assumptions. If this looks good I'll circulate a version with explicit milestones and a DocuSign package.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_StratusHealth_v1.xlsx (type: xlsx, stub)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-04-19T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP for Dedicated/Private (GPU lead times)

Quick internal alignment —

Tessa, Neha, a few sizing/ops notes from infra:
- The 8-node H100-equivalent baseline is reasonable for 250K monthly token peaks if requests are well-sharded. Recommend we size for sustained concurrency 60–80 rps with 2s p95 latency target. If Stratus will use longer contexts (2–4K tokens), we should add +2 nodes to the baseline.
- Lead time caveats: 10–12 weeks assumes no custom rack/airflow requirements and a standard vendor SLA. For Private (on‑prem), we need their cabling/PDUs confirmed — that can add 2–4 weeks.
- Pre-provision suggestion: open a partial tranche (4 nodes) as an early access lane to start evals while the remaining tranche is provisioning — reduces time-to-eval and lowers risk.

I'll drop comments into the workbook where I flagged capacity assumptions.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-04-20T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP for Dedicated/Private (GPU lead times)

Internal follow-up — details for the MAP (assuming Stratus will accept staged tranches):
- Staged tranche plan: Tranche A (4 nodes) delivery target 8–10 weeks; Tranche B (remaining 4 nodes) delivered 6 weeks after Tranche A.
- Acceptance gates and test sets: provide a 3-day perf runbook (we'll supply scripts) and a regression prompt-set for their QA (we should include a small retention of KV cache warmups).
- Credits and SLA: propose time-boxed remediation (7 business days) for performance regressions >10%; if not remediated, 20% credit for impacted tokens for the first billing month. Legal should sign off but this gives procurement a starting position.

I'll prepare the tranche dates and add them to the workbook. Also adding SOC2 evidence link and the standard onboarding checklist.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stratushealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@stratushealth.com>, procurement@stratushealth.com
Date: 2025-04-22T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MAP for Dedicated/Private (GPU lead times)

Tessa —

This looks actionable and close to what procurement needs. Two quick asks before we take to legal: 
1) Can you add an explicit escrow-style clause for tranche delivery: if Tranche A misses target by >14 days, Stratus can defer Tranche B and receive a 10% invoice holdback credit until capacity is restored?
2) Please include a short bullet about security evidence transfer timeline (SOC2 docs) and a named contact for post-signature onboarding.

If you can update the workbook with those bullets and send back, we will circulate to legal today. If it helps, Sara and I are available for a 20-minute call this Friday.

Agree to the staged tranche approach — the partial-tranche for eval is good. Please include the DocuSign package when you send the next version.

Best,
Daniel
